events.extended_summary: Naomi Tekea Craig, a 34-year-old former music teacher from Mandurah, Western Australia, was sentenced to eight-and-a-half years in prison after pleading guilty to 12 child sex offences. The court heard she sexually abused a 12-year-old student over more than a year between August 2024 and December 2025. She met the boy at Frederick Irwin Anglican School where she taught music, later driving him to his new school and keeping a key to his home. Craig was caught after the boy's mother installed CCTV cameras that recorded the abuse. She gave birth to the boy's daughter in January and will be eligible for parole after serving six years and six months. The court heard she manipulated the vulnerable child by sending explicit images and threatening to cancel gifts. Judge John Prior stated the victim was legally incapable of consent.
events.micro_summary: Music teacher Naomi Tekea Craig was sentenced to eight-and-a-half years in prison for sexually abusing a 12-year-old student.

events.summary: Former music teacher Naomi Tekea Craig, 34, was sentenced to eight-and-a-half years in prison after pleading guilty to 12 child sex offences involving a 12-year-old student she abused for over a year and with whom she had a child.

The charges were filed on Monday, Cebu province prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC. events.extended_summary: The Israeli parliament elected Matan Kahana as the new Knesset speaker on Tuesday with 66 votes in the 120-member chamber, defeating Ofir Katz, the candidate backed by outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc, who received 52 votes. Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, who is working to form the next government and replace Netanyahu, replaces Amir Ohana in the role. The election marks a key step toward rolling back policies passed by Netanyahu's outgoing government following the 27 October parliamentary elections in which Netanyahu lost his majority. Eisenkot's bloc, supported by Jewish-led opposition parties and Arab-led parties, has pledged to undo contentious policies and can now use their majority to advance legislative priorities, including bills to set term limits on the prime minister, form an inquiry into the 7 October 2023 attacks, and reverse laws limiting judicial powers. Eisenkot has up to five more weeks to secure a coalition government.
events.micro_summary: Matan Kahana was elected Knesset speaker with 66 votes, advancing efforts to replace Benjamin Netanyahu.
events.summary: The Israeli parliament elected Matan Kahana as speaker with 66 votes in the 120-member chamber, defeating Benjamin Netanyahu's candidate Ofir Katz with 52 votes and enabling the opposition bloc to advance legislation reversing the outgoing government's policies.

events.extended_summary: US fighter jets conducted new “self-defense” strikes Tuesday, using “precision munitions” to target an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island, according to an American military official. The strike “was in response to IRGC aggression targeting American personnel and assets,” the official said, noting that US Central Command remains “highly vigilant and fully postured to protect Americans across the region.” Iranian state media reported that an area on the outskirts of a city on Qeshm Island had been targeted in an “enemy attack.” The deputy governor of Hormozgan province for political and security affairs Ahmad Nafisi said the strike caused no damage to vital infrastructure, commercial or residential areas. Tuesday’s strikes appear similar to others in recent weeks around the Strait of Hormuz, which US officials have also characterized as defensive in nature, rather than marking a significant escalation by American forces. events.micro_summary: US strikes Qeshm Island after Iran targets American base in Bahrain.

events.extended_summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels advanced down Yemen's Red Sea coast, forcing the Saudi-backed internationally recognised government to withdraw its forces from the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait and parts of Marib. The government stated the repositioning was necessary to break the siege of Taiz and protect Aden, where it is based. Saudi Arabia responded by replacing coalition commander Lt Gen Fahd bin Abdulaziz al-Salman with Gen Fayyad bin Hamed bin Ruqad al-Ruwaili. The Houthi advance culminated in a formal withdrawal of government forces, including Southern Giants Brigades, who redeployed to al-Suqyah, 95 miles west of Aden. More than 300,000 civilians have been displaced. The Southern Transitional Council accused Saudi Arabia of incompetence, warning that without a consolidated strategy the Houthis would exploit the lack of unified command. The retreat followed a Saudi-backed military campaign launched 42 days earlier that failed to drive the rebels back.
events.micro_summary: Houthi rebels forced Saudi-backed Yemeni forces to withdraw from the Bab al-Mandab strait, displacing over 300,000 civilians.
events.summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels advanced down Yemen's Red Sea coast, forcing Saudi-backed government forces to withdraw from the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait to defend Aden and Taiz, displacing more than 300,000 civilians and prompting Saudi Arabia to replace its coalition commander.

events.extended_summary: At the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, proponents are pushing for carbon dioxide removal (CDR) to be recognized in the final text. CDR involves extracting heat-trapping carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and storing it underground, in oceans, or in products. A pavilion called Think Negative promotes dramatic increases in carbon removal to address imminent overshoot of temperature thresholds. Meanwhile, a record 700 lobbyists are advocating for carbon capture and storage (CCS), which captures carbon at polluting facilities. On Friday, both CCS and CDR were included for the first time in a text informing the final deal. The UN has acknowledged the world will soon surpass a 1.5C temperature rise, and advocates are pressing Turkey and Australia, the summit's co-presidents, to include CDR in the final outcome while seeking to create a new global agency to coordinate removals.
events.micro_summary: Carbon dioxide removal technologies were included for the first time in COP31 draft text amid a push by 700 lobbyists.
events.summary: At the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, carbon dioxide removal and carbon capture technologies were included in draft text for the first time, as 700 lobbyists pushed for their recognition in the final deal.

events.extended_summary: Nigeria faces one of the world's largest education deficits, with estimates placing between 10.5 million and nearly 19 million children outside formal schooling, roughly one in four of the country's school-age children. The crisis stems from poverty, insecurity, displacement and child marriage, with Jigawa, Kano and Katsina accounting for nearly 30 per cent of the total. In Kano, an estimated 875,593 children aged five to eighteen are out of school despite 99.6 per cent of caregivers valuing education. Cases include a partially blind fourteen-year-old who enrolled only after a one-week attendance test, a fifteen-year-old who left school at thirteen to marry, and a twelve-year-old who now begs to feed siblings after her father was killed. A Hausa-language educational programme has launched via radio, television and social media.
events.micro_summary: Nearly 19 million Nigerian children are out of school amid poverty, insecurity and child marriage.
events.summary: Nigeria has nearly 19 million out-of-school children, one in four of its school-age population, driven by poverty, displacement and child marriage, with Jigawa, Kano and Katsina accounting for nearly 30 per cent of the total.

events.extended_summary: South Africa secured a 2-1 victory over hosts Kenya at Nyayo National Stadium in Nairobi on Tuesday evening in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualification campaign. Relebohile Mofokeng scored both goals for Bafana Bafana, finding the net in the 68th and 86th minutes. South Africa dominated the first half but were denied by Kenya goalkeeper Bryne Odhiambo Omondi, who made several notable saves. The breakthrough came in the 68th minute when Mofokeng capitalized on a defensive error during a counter-attack. He doubled the lead in the 86th minute after receiving a pass from Lyle Foster, dummying a defender before scoring. The win moves South Africa to the top of Group D, one point ahead of Guinea, in the race for the group's single qualification berth. Kenya had already secured qualification as co-hosts of the tournament.
events.micro_summary: South Africa defeated Kenya 2-1 in AFCON qualifiers with Relebohile Mofokeng scoring both goals.
events.summary: South Africa beat Kenya 2-1 at Nyayo National Stadium in Nairobi in 2027 AFCON qualifiers, with Relebohile Mofokeng scoring both goals to put Bafana Bafana top of Group D ahead of Guinea.

events.extended_summary: Wales ended their Nations League group campaign with a 3-2 defeat against 10-man Portugal in Cardiff. Bruno Fernandes opened the scoring after 11 minutes, but David Brooks equalised for Wales with his ninth international goal. Sorba Thomas put Wales ahead before halftime, only for Pedro Neto to level before the break. Substitute Carlos Forbs scored the winner for Portugal in the final quarter, and Neto was subsequently sent off after receiving two yellow cards in two minutes. Wales finished bottom of League A4 with one win and five defeats, guaranteeing a relegation play-off in March, while Portugal topped the group and advanced to the quarter-finals. The match marked Portugal's first victory since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement and Danny Ward's 50th appearance for Wales.
events.micro_summary: Wales lost 3-2 to 10-man Portugal in their Nations League group finale in Cardiff.
events.summary: Wales lost 3-2 to 10-man Portugal in Cardiff, finishing bottom of Nations League Group A4 with a relegation play-off in March, while Portugal topped the group and advanced to the quarter-finals.

events.extended_summary: The Perth Bears will host Manly at Perth Stadium in round one of the 2027 NRL season, marking the club's inaugural game and renewing a rivalry with the Sea Eagles that dates back to 1947. The fixture comes 25 years after the collapse of the Northern Eagles merger. The 2027 campaign begins in Las Vegas with Parramatta facing Gold Coast and Melbourne playing Wests Tigers. On Australian soil, reigning premiers Sydney Roosters will face Brisbane on March 4, while Scott Drinkwater's St George Illawarra meets his former club North Queensland. Newcastle will clash with minor premier Penrith at Newcastle International Sports Centre, Dolphins will host Cronulla in Redcliffe, and Canberra will face South Sydney to close the round. Mal Meninga will coach the Bears in their first season. Perth had hoped to open against South Sydney but scheduling constraints made that impossible.
events.micro_summary: Perth Bears will face Manly in their inaugural NRL game in round one of the 2027 season.

events.extended_summary: World Rugby has suspended South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus for six international matches with immediate effect following comments about match officials after the Springboks' 21-19 defeat to France in the Nations Championship in Paris. During a press conference, Erasmus criticized television match official Matteo Liperini, claiming 17 knee-drop tackles by France went unpunished, with 11 penalisable and three meeting the yellow card threshold. An independent three-person panel chaired by Adam Casseldon SC determined the comments constituted serious misconduct and an unacceptable attack on officials' credibility. The suspension means Erasmus will miss the remainder of the Nations Championship and the first four matches of the 2027 international season. This marks his third sanction, following a 10-month ban in 2021 for comments about referee Nic Berry and a two-match suspension for remarks about Wayne Barnes. The South African Rugby Union has requested a full misconduct hearing to appeal the decision.
events.micro_summary: Rassie Erasmus suspended for six matches after criticizing officials following South Africa's 21-19 loss to France.
events.summary: World Rugby suspended South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus for six international matches after he criticized match officials following the Springboks' 21-19 loss to France, claiming 17 illegal tackles went unpunished. SA Rugby has requested a full hearing.

events.extended_summary: Ukrainian forces executed a complex, multi-stage operation to destroy a key section of the Kerch Bridge connecting occupied Crimea to Russia. After weeks of systematically destroying air defense systems, radars, and electronic warfare assets, Ukrainian units launched waves of drones and missiles. A preliminary strike on November 16 damaged the arch but left it standing. In the early hours of November 17, final strikes using Ukrainian-made Flamingo missiles and other long-range weaponry caused the massive 227-meter road arch, weighing thousands of tonnes, to collapse into the Kerch Strait. The operation involved the 7th Deep Strike Centre and Magyar's Birds brigade, who launched kamikaze drones from central Ukraine. The bridge, opened by Vladimir Putin in 2018 as a prestige project, had been described by Russian propagandists as impregnable. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would be rebuilt and be even better than before.
events.micro_summary: Ukrainian forces collapsed the Kerch Bridge's 227-meter road arch into the sea on November 17 using missiles and drones.
events.summary: Ukrainian forces launched a multi-stage attack on the Kerch Bridge, collapsing a 227-meter road arch into the Kerch Strait on November 17 after a preliminary drone strike on November 16.

events.extended_summary: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands announced plans to open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda, with a return hub expected to accept transfers in 2027. The scheme targets migrants staying illegally who have exhausted legal avenues, with the first phase limited to single men. Deportees will be able to integrate into Rwandan society with rights to residence, education, healthcare and work, or return to their home countries. The five nations stated the plan complies with EU and international law and aims to relieve asylum systems and stop human traffickers. However, human rights groups and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez criticized the plan, with Sánchez stating it has no future or humanity. The initiative follows a recent EU reform allowing return hubs outside the bloc, unlike the scrapped UK scheme that never took effect.
events.micro_summary: Five EU countries plan to open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda by 2027.
events.summary: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands will open a return hub in Rwanda in 2027 to deport rejected asylum seekers, starting with single men, despite human rights criticism.

events.extended_summary: US intelligence indicates Iran is developing specific plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, DC. The plotting includes specific locations and targets and has prompted a flurry of US contingency planning and meetings, though officials characterize it as giving Iran options rather than signaling an imminent attack. The White House stated there are currently no credible threats to the homeland, while President Trump warned Iran would pay a severe price if it attacked. Iran's foreign ministry denied the allegations as baseless. The intelligence emerges as Iran faces ongoing US military strikes and an economic blockade, and follows the Secret Service moving Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to military housing. US intelligence also intercepted claims of bomb-making materials stashed inside the United States, though officials remain divided on that specific credibility.
events.micro_summary: US intelligence reports Iran is planning a dirty bomb attack on Trump officials in Washington.
events.summary: US intelligence indicates Iran is developing specific plans to target senior Trump administration officials with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, DC, prompting contingency planning despite no current credible threat to the homeland.

events.extended_summary: A Panama-flagged tanker, MT TARA GAS, was attacked twice in the Strait of Hormuz on 16 November 2026, sustaining significant damage and catching fire. The first strike caused an engine room fire, while a second attack later left the vessel engulfed in flames. Of the 24 Indian nationals aboard, 21 were safely evacuated to Khasab, Oman, two were injured and admitted to hospital, and one remains missing. India's ministry of external affairs condemned the attack, stating that targeting commercial shipping poses a serious threat to civilian seafarers and calling for free navigation through international waterways. The Iranian Navy confirmed the tanker sustained significant damage, accusing it of travelling in a restricted zone with its navigation switched off. The Strait of Hormuz, through which around 20% of the world's oil shipments travel, has become a focal point of tension since the Iran war began in February.
events.micro_summary: A Panama-flagged tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, leaving one Indian seafarer missing and two injured.
events.summary: A Panama-flagged tanker was struck twice in the Strait of Hormuz, causing fires and leaving one of 24 Indian crew members missing, two injured, and 21 evacuated safely to Khasab, Oman.

events.extended_summary: India's music industry generated Rs 17,401 crore in gross economic value in 2025, a 45% increase from Rs 12,047 crore in 2023. Digital platforms accounted for 52% of this value, followed by broadcasting at 21%, concerts and events at 16%, and filmed entertainment at 11%. The core music segment of labels and publishers grew 7% to Rs 5,433 crore and is projected to reach Rs 7,160 crore by 2028. Music consumption reached nearly six trillion streams in 2025, with 233 million streamers but only 14.4 million paying subscribers, up from seven million in 2023. Independent music comprised 43% of digital consumption. Publishing and performance revenues rose to Rs 1,125 crore from Rs 628 crore in 2023, while the organised workforce expanded 50% to 60,000-70,000 people and annual original song releases reached 22,000-27,000.
events.micro_summary: India's music industry gross value rose 45% to Rs 17,401 crore in 2025.
events.summary: India's music industry generated Rs 17,401 crore in gross economic value in 2025, up 45% from 2023, driven by digital platforms accounting for 52% of value and nearly six trillion streams, though only 14.4 million were paying subscribers.

events.extended_summary: India and the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations emphasized the need for peace, stability and regional cooperation in energy, renewable resources and the green economy at the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit in Manila. Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that India and ASEAN represent nearly one-fourth of the world's population and stressed that the world needs peace, stability and predictability, urging that the future be shaped by cooperation not competition. He affirmed India's unwavering commitment to ASEAN unity and centrality, saying the meeting would take their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to new heights. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos called for closer cooperation in maritime security, environmental protection and blue economy, while welcoming strengthened economic ties through investment and trade facilitation, including review of the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement. Both leaders looked forward to cooperation on renewable energy, energy efficiency, the ASEAN power grid, cybersecurity, sustainable infrastructure and the green economy.
events.micro_summary: India and ASEAN emphasized peace and regional cooperation at the 23rd summit in Manila.
events.summary: India and ASEAN stressed peace, stability and cooperation in energy and green economy at the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit in Manila, with leaders representing nearly one-fourth of world population pledging to shape the future through cooperation.

events.extended_summary: Meghalaya Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma is pursuing a vision to establish Shillong as India's next Artificial Intelligence Valley, a goal he has held since 2008. Speaking at an AI job fair organized with the Department of Education and MSSDS, Sangma emphasized the need for industry collaboration, skilled manpower development, and robust infrastructure including reliable power, connectivity, and logistics facilities to attract global technology companies. The initiative has already identified 125 job openings at Shamrock AI's Shillong office, with the company announcing six specific positions open to freshers including Agentic AI Engineer, SAP S/4HANA AI Automation Analyst, AI Quality and Validation Analyst, Technical Writer, DevOps/MLOps Engineer, and UI/UX Designer. Shamrock AI, which employs over 1,000 people globally, plans to establish a Global Capability Centre in Meghalaya's proposed AI Valley. The government aims to create high-value employment for local youth, enabling them to access technology jobs without migrating, while building industry density to mitigate risks for incoming companies.
events.micro_summary: Meghalaya Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma aims to establish Shillong as India's next AI Valley with 125 initial jobs.
events.summary: Meghalaya Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma announced plans to transform Shillong into India's next Artificial Intelligence Valley, launching an AI job fair that identified 125 job openings at Shamrock AI's Shillong office to create local employment opportunities.

events.extended_summary: India defeated Pakistan 2-1 in the SAFF Championship final at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, securing a record-extending 10th title and becoming the first team to win three successive editions. Suhail Ahmad Bhat equalized in the 60th minute before Sandip Mandi scored an 88th-minute header to complete a dramatic comeback against 10-man Pakistan, who had taken the lead through Alamgir Ghazi's curling finish in first-half stoppage time. Pakistan, appearing in their first SAFF Championship final, were reduced to ten men after Junaid Shah's dismissal following a VAR review. The Blue Tigers had struggled in the first half but found the decisive moment with two minutes remaining.
events.micro_summary: India beat Pakistan 2-1 to win a record 10th SAFF Championship title.
events.summary: India defeated Pakistan 2-1 in the SAFF Championship final in Dhaka on November 17, 2026, with Sandip Mandi scoring an 88th-minute winner to secure a record-extending 10th title and third consecutive crown.

events.extended_summary: India's Under-17 men's team defeated Palestine 4-1 in Group E of the AFC U17 Asian Cup 2027 Qualifiers in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday, remaining unbeaten in the group. Kamgouhao Doungel opened the scoring in the eighth minute after capitalizing on an error by Palestine's Mohammed Jamhour, who was sent off two minutes later for a dangerous challenge. Palestine equalized through Yazan Khalifah's penalty in the 32nd minute, but India regained the lead in the 52nd minute through Mukundo Singh Ningthoujam. Captain Dallalmoun Gangte scored in the 59th minute, and Zoramdinthara Lalhunmawia added a fourth in the 89th minute. The match was suspended for over two hours due to heavy rain before the second half. India now needs a point from their final match against hosts Malaysia to qualify for the U17 Asian Cup, though qualification could be secured earlier if Malaysia fail to beat Guam.
events.micro_summary: India U17 defeated Palestine 4-1 in AFC U17 Asian Cup 2027 qualifiers despite rain and incidents.
events.summary: India's U17 team beat Palestine 4-1 in AFC U17 Asian Cup 2027 qualifiers in Kuala Lumpur, with goals from Doungel, Singh, Gangte and Lalhunmawia, despite heavy rain delays and a red card for Palestine.

events.extended_summary: India begin a two-Test series against New Zealand on Thursday at Basin Reserve in Wellington, with captain Shubman Gill confirming the team will field four fast bowlers. Jasprit Bumrah is a certain starter, while Mohammed Siraj, Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj, Prasidh Krishna and Gurnoor Brar compete for the remaining three spots. Bowling coach Morne Morkel stated the final decision on the pace attack would depend on conditions, with strong winds expected to challenge both teams. India enter the series following a 3-1 victory in the recent ODI series, having previously drawn 2-2 with England, won 1-0 against Sri Lanka and lost 0-2 to South Africa at home. The series holds significance for the World Test Championship final and for Gill's captaincy.
events.micro_summary: India will play four fast bowlers in the first Test against New Zealand starting Thursday in Wellington.
events.summary: India captain Shubman Gill confirmed his team will play four fast bowlers in the two-Test series against New Zealand starting Thursday at Basin Reserve in Wellington, with Jasprit Bumrah a sure starter and strong winds expected.

events.extended_summary: Defending champion India will face Pakistan in the SAFF Championship 2026 final at the National Stadium in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on Tuesday, November 17, with kickoff at 7:30 PM IST. India, seeking a historic third consecutive title, has won a record nine championships in 1993, 1997, 1999, 2005, 2009, 2011, 2015, 2021 and 2023 but has never secured three successive editions. Pakistan appears in its first-ever SAFF Championship final after defeating hosts Bangladesh 1-0 in the semifinals on Saturday, having previously reached the last four on four occasions, most recently in 2018. The match will not be televised in India and will be available via live streaming on the Veto app and website.
events.micro_summary: India seeks third straight SAFF title against Pakistan in 2026 final after Pakistan's 1-0 semifinal victory.
events.summary: Defending champion India will face Pakistan in the SAFF Championship 2026 final at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Tuesday, November 17 at 7:30 PM IST, with Pakistan reaching its first final after defeating Bangladesh 1-0.

events.extended_summary: The Mahindra XEV 9S electric SUV secured a 5-star safety rating in Bharat NCAP crash tests, earning top marks in both adult and child occupant protection categories. The vehicle scored 31.15 out of 32 points for Adult Occupant Protection, including 15.15/16 in the frontal offset deformable barrier test at 64 kmph and a perfect 16/16 in the side movable deformable barrier test at 50 kmph. Protection ratings for the driver and passenger were predominantly 'Good' across head, neck, chest, thighs, pelvis, and feet. For Child Occupant Protection, the SUV achieved 45 out of 49 points, with perfect 12/12 scores for both 18-month-old and 3-year-old child dummies in dynamic and CRS installation tests. The XEV 9S comes equipped with six airbags as standard (seven in higher trims), tyre pressure monitoring, ISOFIX mounts, and ESP, while top-spec variants include a comprehensive ADAS suite featuring automatic emergency braking and lane keep assist.
events.micro_summary: Mahindra XEV 9S electric SUV secures 5-star Bharat NCAP safety rating with 31.15/32 adult and 45/49 child protection scores.
events.summary: The Mahindra XEV 9S electric SUV achieved a 5-star safety rating in Bharat NCAP crash tests, scoring 31.15/32 for adult occupant protection and 45/49 for child occupant protection, with six airbags and advanced safety features standard.

events.micro_summary: Kaziranga accident: Injured toddler returns home to grandparents in Kaliabor as parents undergo treatment in Jorhat.

events.extended_summary: Two people were killed and three others seriously injured in a head-on collision between two motorcycles near Bajpur village on the Manjhanpur-Udhihin road in Uttar Pradesh's Kaushambi district at around 11:30 pm on Monday. The deceased were identified as Samar Singh, 24, a resident of Charwa, and Hansraj Yadav, 40, from Faridaganj village. Singh was travelling with a friend, while Yadav's 13-year-old son and another person were riding with him. All five occupants sustained serious injuries and were taken to the district hospital, where both riders succumbed to their injuries. The three other injured, including Yadav's son, were referred to SRN Hospital in Prayagraj for treatment. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem examination. Two youths on one motorcycle were going to a function while three youths were coming from the opposite direction when the collision occurred.
events.micro_summary: Two motorcyclists were killed and three injured in a head-on collision in Kaushambi district.
events.summary: Two motorcyclists were killed and three others injured in a head-on collision near Bajpur village in Kaushambi district on Monday night. The deceased were identified as Samar Singh, 24, and Hansraj Yadav, 40.
